bug_semantics: A remote discovery report can carry a 255-byte EIR/advertising-data block whose first name element has field_len 254, so eir_parse derives data_len 253 and passes it to name2utf8. name2utf8 copies len attacker-controlled bytes with strncpy into utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2], only 250 bytes because HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248. The resulting three-byte stack overwrite can crash bluetoothd and can also leave the local array unterminated for subsequent strtoutf8/g_strstrip/g_strdup reads, with potential code execution depending on the build and architecture.
flaw_origin: Commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 changed EIR name handling from rejecting invalid UTF-8 and safely g_strndup-ing accepted data to routing it through a newly added name2utf8 function. That new EIR-specific function introduced the fixed 250-byte stack buffer and the attacker-sized strncpy without a length clamp. Although the subject says 'Move', this is not a mere relocation of an already-vulnerable EIR sink: the parent has no name2utf8 in src/eir.c and rejects malformed EIR names; the copied event.c pattern used a fixed MGMT_MAX_NAME_LENGTH count rather than the EIR element's variable len.
ai_marker: No AI marker. `git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` shows human author and committer Johan Hedberg <johan.hedberg@intel.com> and only the message `core: Move UTF-8 validation of device names into eir.c`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: Upstream first-party advisory https://github.com/bluez/bluez/security/advisories/GHSA-68h6-5qgp-3975 identifies CVE-2026-80186, src/eir.c:name2utf8, a remotely supplied EIR name, field_len 254/data_len 253, the 250-byte stack buffer, affected version 5.86, and patched commit 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2.

At 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^, `git grep -n HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH -- lib/bluetooth/hci.h src/eir.c` shows HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH is 248 and name2utf8 declares `char utf8_name[HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH + 2]`; `git blame -L 136,150 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/eir.c` attributes the buffer, memset, attacker-sized `strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)`, strip, and duplicate lines to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22.

`git blame -L 250,306 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/eir.c` reproduces the length path: uint8_t field_len, `len += field_len + 1`, only an aggregate `len > eir_len` rejection, `data_len = field_len - 1`, and name fields passed as `name2utf8(data, data_len)`. `git grep -n -C 25 'btd_adapter_device_found(adapter, &ev->addr.bdaddr' 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -- src/adapter.c` shows the remote MGMT Device Found event supplies its eir/eir_len to the discovery path, and the callee's data_len is uint8_t, permitting 255.

`git log 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2^ -L ':name2utf8:src/eir.c'` and `git log master --reverse -S 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' -- src/eir.c` both reach 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 as the first writer of the vulnerable EIR sink; the later 218db700f49370bc07ce1e6d609d28d846470d99 only removes the valid-UTF-8 fast path and changes conversion, while the unsafe buffer and variable-length copy remain attributed to 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22.

`git show --find-renames --find-copies 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` shows the newly added name2utf8 and the name-case call replacing the parent's validation/g_strndup path. `git rev-parse 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22^` returns 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e; `git grep -n -e name2utf8 -e 'strncpy(utf8_name, (char *) name, len)' 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e -- src/eir.c` has no match, while `git grep -n -C 6 g_utf8_validate 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e -- src/eir.c` shows malformed names were rejected and accepted names used g_strndup.

Release ancestry establishes the source boundary: `git describe --contains --match='5.*' 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` returns `5.0~2624`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeds for introducer versus 5.0^{} and fails versus 4.101^{}, so the unsafe source first shipped in 5.0. This is broader than the advisory UI's explicit affected-version entry of 5.86. The fix was committed after both 5.86 and 5.87: ancestry fails for 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2 versus 5.87^{}, and `git tag --contains 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2` is empty in the validated clone, so no observed release tag contains the fix yet.

`git show --format=fuller 381b5d0d208972586282116d333865ba93b8dec2` is the direct repair: it adds `len = MIN(len, HCI_MAX_NAME_LENGTH);` immediately before memset/strncpy and changes no other file. Thus the advisory fix and the smallest direct fix are the same commit.

`git cat-file commit 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22` provides the BIC-only provenance check: tree 2650a41bd430d9a9acb38ece9975d5bb5630df6e, parent 0f75430e0c827ad069f616e02563237b1099518e, human author/committer Johan Hedberg, and no AI/bot marker or trailer. Any AI assistance recorded on the 2026 fix is outside the protocol's BIC-only judgment.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the unbounded copy in the EIR name conversion sink, not the 2025 conversion refactor and not the 2026 fix. Line history and pickaxe agree that 155fa21473ada6d3e7773175186badd4bc0fde22 first wrote the fixed stack array plus variable-length copy and first routed EIR names through it. Its direct parent has neither the sink nor the vulnerable route, instead rejecting invalid UTF-8 and using a bounded allocation, so parent absence is directly proven. The commit is a normal 2012 human-authored commit object with no AI disclosure or bot identity. Under the required BIC-only rule the closed verdict is therefore NOT_AI.
